newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FOCUS-Hungary bank panic may be political - FinMin.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Hungary bank panic may be political - FinMin.

text.p: Panic withdrawals from Postabank, one of Hungary's largest banks, may have been triggered by the government's political opponents and by competitors, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.
Thousands of people queued outside Postabank branches to withdraw their money after rumours circulated that the bank had been hit by big losses.
Postabank chairman Gabor Princz told a news conference that a rival bank reduced its lending ceiling to Postabank on the interbank market recently -- a possible sign of falling confidence.

Other banking sources said they had heard reports that Postabank was trying to cut costs, including reducing its number of mobile phones, which might have been interpreted as a sign of financial trouble.

But the bank, Finance Ministry and banking authority officials denied that Postabank was in difficulty -- even with the run on deposits -- and told a hastily gathered news conference that it would be able to pay out all its clients.
"We have the fairly well-justified suspicion that this was an organised action against the bank," Finance Ministry Secretary of State Laszlo Akar said.
"This came after the agricultural demonstrations, in a time when the situation is tense," he said. "You should think about if such large coincidences can happen."
Thousands of farmers blocked lanes on several of Hungary's main roads from Monday in protest against tax burdens.
It was the most serious demonstration against the Socialist-Liberal government coalition since the last election in 1994.
Imre Tarafas, chairman of the State Banking and Capital Markets Supervision body, said Postabank's financial situation could not justify the panic withdrawals.

A regular supervision investigation at the bank in the second half of 1996 did not find any irregularities which could threaten its safe operations and Postabank was able to repay its depositors, he said.

"Postabank has assets of 70 billion forints ($400 million) which can be liquidated quickly and also further moveable assets," he said, adding he did not see any chance that the supervision body should freeze Postabank's accounts.
Princz said Postabank kept retail deposits totalling 200 billion forints and had created all the provisions needed for safe banking operations while still posting profits.

He added that Postabank boosted its assets by 40 percent last year, moving up from the number three to second position in Hungary, and had four million deposits in a country which has a population of slightly more than 10 million.
Princz said Postabank was aware of rumours circulating about its difficulties in the past few weeks.
He added that such rumours had appeared several times since the bank was founded nine years ago but it had never experienced such panic withdrawals as now.

"This wave surprised, appalled us," he said, adding that some of the branches might run out of money temporarily, which might lead to conflicts with customers. But the bank would be able to supply the branches with cash continuously.
"I hope that people will cool in a few days, when they see that we are paying and there is no trouble," he added. ($ = 175.5 Hungarian Forints)
